  Staff respectfully recommends that the City Council of the City of Lynwood approve the warrant
  registers dated August 3, 2021 for FY 2020-2021 and FY 2021-2022.

  7.  CITY MANAGER'S MONTHLY TASK ORDER REPORT
  Comments:
  On September 17, 2019, the City Council of the City of Lynwood approved Ordinance No. 1727,
  "An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Lynwood, County of Los Angeles, State of
  California Amending Section 6-3.16 of the Lynwood Municipal Code," which allows for a set
  spending authority allotted for City Management or his/her authorized designee. Pursuant to the
  amended Municipal Code, the City Manager must provide a monthly report to the City Council of
  purchases executed under his/her authority. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  It is recommended that the City Council of the City of Lynwood receive and file the City Manager's
  Monthly Task Order Report for the month of July 2021.

  8.  CONSIDER APPROVAL OF AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT FOR THE
  AMERICAN RESCUE PLAN ACT COORDINATOR
  Comments:
  The United States Treasury rolled out its interim final rule on State and local fiscal recovery funds
  on May 10, 2021. All municipalities have until the end of 2024 to obligate received funds, but have
  until end of 2026 to spend the funds. The ARPA Coordinator will track, categorize, and assist the
  City in compliance with ARPA requirements. (CM)

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve an at-will employment agreement for the
  American Rescue Plan Act Coordinator and authorize the City Manager sign said agreement on
  behalf of the City of Lynwood on a form approved by the City Attorney.

  9.  CONSIDER APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH KILEY &
  ASSOCIATES, LLC, FOR FEDERAL LEGISLATIVE ADVOCACY SERVICES

City Council Special Meeting - Page 2 of 57
   Comments:
  The City is seeking to hire a qualified firm to provide federal legislative advocacy services for the City.
  The City currently has no contracted firms to do such services. Staff is recommending Kiley &
  Associates based upon the professional experience of the firm, the strategic location of the firm in
  Washington, D.C., and the familiarity of the firm with the City of Lynwood. The cost proposal from Kiley
  & Associates includes an annual not-to-exceed consideration of $60,000.00 with a monthly rate of
  $5,000.00. Locally, Kiley & Associates also provides federal legislative advocacy services to the cities of
  South Gate and Carson.

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve a contract services agreement with Kiley &
  Associates, LLC, for Federal Legislative Advocacy Services; and authorize the City Manager
  sign a two-year agreement on behalf of the City of Lynwood on a form approved by the City
  Attorney.

  10.  PROJECT ACCEPTANCE OF BREWSTER AVENUE STREET AND WATER
  IMPROVEMENT PROJECT, PROJECT (CIP NO. 4011.68.079)
  Comments:
  The construction on Brewster Avenue Street and Water Improvement Project started on June 1,
  2020. The final inspection and project completion was on November 25, 2020. Staff conducted
  the final inspection on November 25, 2020 and found that all work was completed in accordance
  with the project plans and specifications. The Project is ready for acceptance.

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING THE BREWSTER
  AVENUE STREET AND WATER IMPROVEMENT PROJECT (CIP NO. 4011.68.079) AS
  COMPLETE; AUTHORIZATION THE FILING OF THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION WITH
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE RELEASE OF THE
  5% RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE ACCEPTANCE.”

  11.  PROJECT ACCEPTANCE OF LONG BEACH BLVD/ 105 FWY INTERCHANGE
  CURB RAMPS PROJECT (CIP NO. 4011.68.062)
  Comments:
  The construction on the Long Beach Blvd/ 105 Fwy Interchange Curb Ramps Project started on
  January 20, 2021. The final inspection and project completion was on February 20, 2021. Staff
  conducted the final inspection on February 20, 2021 and found that all work was completed in
  accordance with the project plans and specifications. The Project is ready for acceptance.

  Recommendation:
  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt the attached resolution entitled: “A RESOLUTION
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF LYNWOOD ACCEPTING THE LONG BEACH
  BLVD/ 105 FWY INTERCHANGE CURB RAMPS PROJECT (CIP NO. 4011.68.062) AS
  COMPLETE; AUTHORIZING THE FILING OF THE NOTICE OF COMPLETION WITH
  THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY RECORDER’S OFFICE AND THE RELEASE OF THE
  5% RETENTION 35 DAYS AFTER THE ACCEPTANCE.”

  Background:

  The United States Treasury rolled out its interim final rule on State and local fiscal recovery funds on May 10,
  2021. All municipalities have until the end of 2024 to obligate received funds, but have until end of 2026 to spend
  the funds. The ARPA Coordinator will track, categorize, and assist the City in compliance with ARPA
  requirements.

  ARPA is intended to help communities prospectively, but there are three exceptions:

  2) Assistance to households and small businesses
  3) The calculation of lost revenue

  Per the United States Treasury, these funds will substantially infuse resources to meet pandemic response needs
  and rebuild a stronger and more equitable economy as the country recovers. The ARPA Coordinator will assist in
  managing ARPA funds and monitoring ARPA programs in the following approved categorical areas:

  • Support Public Health Expenditures
  • Address negative economic impacts caused by the public health emergency

  Background:

  As part of the ongoing adjustments and responses to the COVID-19 epidemic, many public sector organizations
  are seeking to contract with lobbyist firms with specific federal associations and experience. The City currently
  contracts for professional lobbyist services at the State level but does not have representation at the federal level.

  representation is provided for City Council discussion and consideration.

  has no contracted firms to do such services. Staff is recommending Kiley & Associates based upon the professional
  experience of the firm, the strategic location of the firm in Washington, D.C., and the familiarity of the firm with the City of
